subject.title: fix(runtime): cancelled workflows no longer continue external commands

question: Should an abort that arrives after a resumed workflow or pipeline has entered execution consume its approval/input/workflow resume capability even when the completed side-effect boundary cannot be inferred by the caller?
rationale: The patch deliberately chooses a durable compatibility and replay-safety policy for persisted resume state; tests can validate the selected behavior but cannot determine the permanent product contract.

options.title: Accept execution-time consumption
options.body: Merge the current policy: preserve pre-aborted retries, but consume resumable state once execution has begun and the parent signal aborts to prevent possible side-effect replay.

options.title: Preserve retries more broadly
options.body: Keep state retryable after more abort cases, accepting that a separate durable side-effect-progress model would be needed before retries can be safe.

recommendation.title: Accept execution-time consumption
recommendation.body: Merge the current policy: preserve pre-aborted retries, but consume resumable state once execution has begun and the parent signal aborts to prevent possible side-effect replay.

likelyOwner.reason: They implemented and documented the proposed cancellation and resume-state boundary, though current-main feature ownership could not be independently traced.
